name: IEC priority encoder (HPRI/BIN)
summary: IEC coder marked HPRI/BIN that outputs the binary number of the highest-priority active input.
description: A priority encoder is shown as an X/Y coder with the qualifier HPRI/BIN: highest priority in, binary out. Inputs are numbered by priority, and outputs carry binary weights. Additional outputs often signal that any input is active, which lets stages be cascaded.

On control drawings priority encoders reduce many alarm or request lines to a code, for example to identify the most important active fault for display. The input numbering must match the intended priority order.
The symbol does not state whether inputs are latched. If the encoder input is a momentary event, a latch stage is needed before it.
readingNotes: Higher input number normally means higher priority.
Look for group-select or any-active outputs used to cascade.
distinction: A plain binary encoder assumes only one input active; HPRI resolves multiple active inputs.
